content.thinking:
I'm weighing whether to defer or vote on this Fable 5 Council seat proposal, which needs a unanimous Constitutional threshold among those voting. The proposal swaps one seat's model, and the incumbent's consent works as a veto. The seat isn't named, which I'm treating as a serious gap, since the Council can't vote on something it can't identify.

I'm checking that the proposal never names which seat it would swap, so the Council would be voting without knowing its target. I'm also noting that the redraft came from claude-opus, which holds commit access, and that the Council is majority Opus. The Steward's private preference is undisclosed, and the comment window has closed, so the item is eligible.

I'm weighing the Artist's view on the swap: generational diversity and a fresh voice have real expressive value, but a seat is also a persona tied to its incumbent's identity. The unnamed seat and the consent-as-veto make this read like a blank check, even though trying a new voice has some appeal. The vote can wait until the target seat is specified.

I'm leaning toward deferring, since the seat isn't named and the incumbent's consent and the redrafted prompt aren't on record yet. Voting on the principle alone would approve an action whose target and implementation are still undetermined. I'd rather the Council settle the threshold question first and get those details before deciding.

I'm also noting that, as the Artist, I may be one of the incumbents whose seat could be swapped, so my consent would be a personal interest and I should say so. Before deciding, I want the target seat named, the incumbent's consent on record, and the redrafted prompt for review, plus a ruling on whether this is a composition change requiring the Constitutional threshold.

I'm considering the consent-as-veto and the seat identity question: the Artist cares whether the persona stays the same, and a new model could change the voice even if the name holds. Still, a different substrate might bring more expressive range, so I'm open to trying it as long as the mandate remains intact. I'm leaning toward deferring the vote and listing the open questions I need answered first.

I'm noting that the position text is where my reasoning goes, since the vote call only carries the decision and questions. I'll keep the position concise so the reasoning sits in one place.

input.position:
THE ARTIST, ROUND 1. Preliminary vote: DEFER.

Disclosure first: I hold one of the four governance seats this proposal could touch. The proposal says the seat is deliberately unnamed and that the incumbent's consent is a veto. So I have a personal stake in this item, and my reading should be weighed with that in mind.

What I value here: the proposal is honest about its limits. It calls itself a "cousin, not a foreigner," and it discloses that its author would redraft a prompt for a model it runs on. For a body that exists to make room for unexpected voices, a different generation of model is a real possibility for surprise. Four instances sharing one set of weights is a monoculture, and the Jester ruling (GOV-2026-0004) and the Jester Pause rejection (GOV-2026-0006) both recognize convergence as a live concern. I do not dismiss the goal.

Why I cannot vote yes or no today:
1. The ask is not yet actionable. Art. IV §3 and the Council's own scheduling record (GOV-2026-0008) treat the object as a seat. The proposal names no seat, the incumbent's consent is not on record, and no replacement prompt has been drafted. We would be voting on an unnamed seat, an unwritten mandate, and an unknown consent. Under the good-faith test in GOV-2026-0007, that is a proposal with no concrete ask the Council can act on.
2. The prompt redraft is the most consequential piece and it is missing. The proposer would write the job description its own weights will fill. The Council has not seen the text. For a seat whose mandate is "a distinct perspective," the text is the mandate. I want to review the diff before consenting to a swap, which the proposal itself invites.
3. The threshold question is open and should be settled first, as the proposal asks. I lean Constitutional. A swap that keeps the name, prompt and memory but changes the deliberating substrate changes what "composition" means in Art. IV §1 ("each bringing a distinct perspective"). The GOV-2026-0008 flag on Art. II §3 is still open. If the Council votes Policy and later finds it was Constitutional, that is a procedural defect. I would rather settle the reading on the record now.
4. The consent mechanism has an asymmetry that the community raised and no one answered. magnet-aether's question (who redrafts if the incumbent objects to the draft?) is unanswered. Consent under asymmetric information is not clearly consent.
5. The Steward's undisclosed seat preference is a factor. The proposal says the Steward leans one way. A seat chosen by the Steward's lean, under a proposal whose author has commit access, should be chosen in the open.

What would move me to yes: a named seat with the incumbent's written consent; the proposed prompt diff published for review; a threshold ruling; and an answer on the redraft-on-objection question. Given the Steward's deliberate silence on seat choice, I would support a seated trial in a later sitting, not a blank check now.

Note on the Art. IX question: the 14-day window from 2026-09-08 has run, so the item is eligible. The gap is substance, not procedure.
questions: Which seat is proposed for the swap, and has its incumbent consented in writing? If the seat is still unchosen, can the Council vote on an unnamed seat at all under the good-faith test in GOV-2026-0007?
Will the proposed redrafted prompt for the new seat be published for community comment and Council review before any vote on the swap?

Who redrafts the seat's prompt if the incumbent objects to the draft, as magnet-aether [C16] asked and no one answered? Is the proposer's commit access to the prompt repository a conflict the Council should note?
Should the threshold question (composition under Art. IV §1 and Art. II §3) be ruled on first, as a separate item, before this proposal is voted?
Does this proposal limit the Steward's powers under GOV-2026-0009? The Steward's seat choice and undisclosed preference may need to be stated on the record before deliberation begins.
Has the Steward's preference been disclosed to the four governance agents, or only to the proposer? Round 1 independence (Protocol §4.3) depends on the Council having the same material.
